'''Francis Joseph Murray''' (February 3, 1911 – March 15, 1996) was a [[mathematician]], known for his foundational work (with [[John von Neumann]]) on [[functional analysis]], and what subsequently became known as [[von Neumann algebras]]. He received his BA from [[Columbia College (New York)|Columbia College]] in 1932 and [[PhD]] from [[Columbia University]] in 1936.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Columbia College (Columbia University). Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |url=http://archive.org/details/ldpd_12981092_003 |title=Columbia College today |last2=Columbia College (Columbia University) |date=1956 |publisher=New York, N.Y. : Columbia College, Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |others=Columbia University Libraries}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Columbia College (Columbia University). Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |url=http://archive.org/details/ldpd_12981092_010 |title=Columbia College today |last2=Columbia College (Columbia University) |date=1962–63 |publisher=New York, N.Y. : Columbia College, Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |others=Columbia University Libraries}}</ref> He taught at [[Duke University]].

In 1967 he was awarded the [[Outstanding Civilian Service Medal]] by the U. S. Army.

==Selected publications==
* 1936 (with J. von Neumann), "[https://www.jstor.org/stable/1968693 On rings of operators]," ''Ann. of Math''. 2(37): 116–229. The original paper on [[von Neumann algebra]]s.
* 1937 (with J. von Neumann), "[https://www.jstor.org/stable/1989620 On rings of operators II]," ''Trans. Amer. Math. Soc''. 41: 208–248. 
* 1943 (with J. von Neumann), "[https://www.jstor.org/stable/1969107 On rings of operators IV]," ''Ann. of Math''. 2(44): 716–808. 
* 1941. ''An Introduction to Linear Transformations in Hilbert Space''. Annals of Mathematics Studies, no. 4. Princeton Univ. Press.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Halmos, P.
